newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - June 20.

text.p: There are 11 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC JOURNAL said that whether Beijing liked it or not, the British administration awakened Hong Kong people's pursuit of freedom and democracy during its last days, changing Hong Kong people's indifference towards politics, and the Special Administrative region government could not turn the clock back, the paper said. Although Governor Chris Patten's future career would be in Europe, his political reforms and his five years in office had brought a pleasant surprise to Hong Kong's democratic development, it said.

-- SING TAO said that Governor Chris Patten failed to communicate with China and take reality into consideration when he carried out his political reforms, although his measures were welcomed by most Hong Kong people. Hong Kong people are grateful for Patten's efforts to develop a democratic system in the territory, but cannot understand why he refused to compromise when he knew that his reforms would not be accepted by the Chinese side after the handover. The paper said Patten could have done a lot better if he had not focused too much on his political reforms and neglected people's livelihood.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said Hong Kong's reputation as the "Pearl of the Orient" was created by Hong Kong people, and was not a result of British colonial rule as indicated by Governor Chris Patten. It said that without Hong Kong people's wisdom and hard work, the territory would not be what it is now. After the handover, Hong Kong would enter a new era under the "one country, two systems" principle, and with its present economic foundation plus the new vitality brought about by the pride of its people becoming their own masters, Hong Kong would have a brighter future, the paper said.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said it would never be easy for Hong Kong authorities to deal with the People's Liberation Army. After the handover, they would have no direct jurisdiction over a garrison that was answerable only to Beijing. However, unless the administration stood by its staff when they came into conflicts with the PLA, the situation would become impossible, the paper said. Customs officers had not received the support they deserved during the incident involving PLA major-general Zhou Borong's complaint, and an unfortunate precedent had been set, it said.
